summary: Ephemeral env bootstrap failing: cross-account role mapping denied after org policy rollout
description:
Issue summary:
Ephemeral environment bootstrap jobs for staging cannot complete because the cross-account role assumption from ops-service to staging-ephemeral-role is being denied after the recent org-level IAM policy rollout on 2026-03-09. This affects automated bootstrapping of ephemeral sandboxes used by infra and SRE for reproducing production load patterns.

Impact:
- New ephemeral environments fail to provision (bootstrap step fails) ~100% of attempts in staging-us-east.
- Blocks debug/playback workflows for infra and platform engineers.
- Affects on-call ability to repro noisy-neighbor and autoscaler issues in realistic envs.

Environment:
- Affected account: aws-production-ops (ops master account) -> aws-staging-ephemeral (staging account) cross-account assume-role path.
- Also observed a separate but related deny on GCP: WIF mapping for ephemeral-runner-sa -> staging-runner-sa failing in eu-west when additional attribute-based deny is applied.
- Staging region: us-east-1; secondary repro in eu-west-1.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger ephemeral provision via infra/ephemeral-runner (CI job infra/ephemeral:provision).
2) Job attempts to assume role arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/staging-ephemeral-role using ops-service principal (arn:aws:iam::555666777888:role/ops-service).
3) AssumeRole API returns AccessDenied with message referencing org policy enforcement.

Observed behavior:
- AWS STS AssumeRole returns HTTP 403 AccessDenied with policy evaluation details: "ExplicitDeny: org policy requires principal to present tag 'environment' as request tag or principal tag."
- Role trust policy appears unchanged; assumption previously worked before org policy rollout.
- GCP WIF exchange returns 403 with message: "Mapping denied by org IAM attribute constraint: attribute 'env' missing."

Expected behavior:
- Ephemeral bootstrap role assumption should succeed for ops-service when bootstrap request includes the environment tag asserted by the short-lived session or principal mapping.

Logs / traces (abridged):
- AWS CloudTrail snippets: 2026-03-10T03:12:45Z AssumeRole for ops-service -> Deny (Condition MissingTag 'environment').
- Staging bootstrap logs: "ERROR: cannot assume staging-ephemeral-role: AccessDenied: External caller does not meet org policy conditions".
- GCP audit log: WIF token exchange denied, attribute.env not present.

Investigation notes so far:
- On 2026-03-09 Security rolled out an org-wide guardrail requiring either aws:PrincipalTag/environment or aws:RequestTag/environment for cross-account assumptions to enforce environment scoping. The rollout PR is linked in related_confluence_pages.
- Ops-service did not start including the session RequestTags on the AssumeRole call. The ephemeral-runner flow relies on pre-existing principal tags on the ops-service role, which were trimmed when we rotated service principals last month.
- Hypothesis A: Org policy expects RequestTag in the STS call and denies if not present; our assume-role wrapper (deploy-scripts) was not updated to forward tags.
- Hypothesis B: The staging-ephemeral-role trust policy was relying on PrincipalTag matching that got removed during a recent role replacement.
- GCP side: WIF attribute mapping expects attribute.env in the token; ephemeral runner flow does not populate attribute mapping for older CI tokens.

Temporary workaround applied:
- Security approved an emergency allowlist for the ops-service principal for a 6-hour window on 2026-03-11 to unblock immediate onboarding and reproduce flows. This was applied to staging accounts only.

Next steps / owners:
- Priya Desai (assignee): Confirm whether deploy-scripts and ephemeral-runner wrappers can start sending aws:RequestTag/environment in STS AssumeRole calls. If so, implement and coordinate a canary deployment. (Owner: Priya)
- Security (cc'd): Revisit org policy requirement text to allow either existing PrincipalTag OR RequestTag for 30-day migration window. (Owner: Security admin)
- Infra/CI: Update ephemeral bootstrap runbook to validate tag propagation and include a sanity check. (Owner: Infra)
- SRE: Recreate repro in a sandbox using the emergency allowlist and capture full trace to verify fix. (Owner: SRE)

Acceptance criteria:
- New ephemeral environments can be provisioned without emergency allowlist and with org policy enforcement active.
- Changes covered by a short canary in staging, then rollout to other accounts.

References:
- https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/6321 (deploy-scripts change proposal)
- https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SEC/pages/5001/org-policy-change-log
investigation_notes:
Summary of tech investigation:
- Confirmed org-level SCP-style deny enforced via org policy service on 2026-03-09.
- ops-service role no longer carries environment principal tag after secret rotation; assume-role wrapper does not set RequestTags.
- Minimal repro created with AWS CLI: sts assume-role --role-arn <staging-role> --role-session-name temp --duration-seconds 900 -> fails without --tags. Succeeds when --tags Key=environment,Value=staging is provided.
- GCP WIF: jwt subject mapping requires attribute 'env' present; token issued by legacy CI runner lacks custom claim.
- Mitigation strategy: add tagging in assume-role wrapper + short migration policy change to accept existing principal tag for 30d.

resolution: Work in progress — canary deployed in staging; emergency allowlist used to unblock flows. Final remediation requires deploy-scripts change and org policy migration exception to be formalized.
resolution_notes: If canary succeeds for 24h, schedule rollouts and rescind emergency allowlist. Post-mortem to capture gaps in role rotation runbook so principal tags are preserved or refreshed as part of rotation.
